title: Bacterial species and antimicrobial resistance differ between catheter and non–catheter-associated urinary tract infections: Data from a national surveillance network

claims.text: E. coli is the most frequent uropathogen in both catheter-associated (CAUTI) and non-catheter-associated UTI.
claims.byte_quote: Escherichia coli was the most frequent pathogen identified in both CAUTI and non-CAUTI samples

claims.text: Four organisms (E. coli, K. pneumoniae, P. aeruginosa, P. mirabilis) make up 70% of CAUTI and 85% of non-CAUTI pathogens.
claims.byte_quote: Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Proteus mirabilis together represented 70% and 85% of pathogens identified in CAUTI and non-CAUTI samples, respectively

claims.text: P. aeruginosa is enriched in catheter-associated UTI (10% of CAUTI vs 3.3% of non-CAUTI).
claims.byte_quote: Pseudomonas aeruginosa represented 10% of CAUTI pathogens versus only 3.3% of non-CAUTIs

claims.text: E. coli proportion: 31.9% in CAUTI vs 54.8% in non-CAUTI.
P. aeruginosa proportion: 10.1% in CAUTI vs 3.3% in non-CAUTI.
K. pneumoniae proportion: 11.1% in CAUTI vs 9.9% in non-CAUTI.
Host/risk factor: CAUTI patients are older (median 75 y) than non-CAUTI patients (median 65 y); catheterization (device) is the differentiating exposure.
claims.byte_quote: Age, median y (IQR): CAUTI 75 (60–80); Non-CAUTI 65 (40–75); P<.001

claims.text: Host/risk factor: CAUTI cases are predominantly male (57.4%), whereas non-CAUTI cases are predominantly female (68.6%).
Catheter association predicts higher resistance to recommended empirical antibiotics.
claims.byte_quote: CAUTI pathogens were more often resistant to recommended empirical antibiotics than non-CAUTI pathogens.

claims.text: E. coli ciprofloxacin (CIP) resistance is higher in CAUTI (26%) than non-CAUTI (16.9%).
claims.byte_quote: 26% of CAUTI samples were resistant vs 16.9% of non-CAUTI samples

claims.text: E. coli third/fourth-generation cephalosporin (C3/4G) resistance: 11.6% CAUTI vs 8.2% non-CAUTI.
claims.byte_quote: 11.6% of CAUTI samples were resistant vs 8.2% of non-CAUTI samples

claims.text: E. coli norfloxacin (NOR) resistance: 28.1% CAUTI vs 19.1% non-CAUTI.
claims.byte_quote: 28.1% of CAUTI samples were resistant vs 19.1% of non-CAUTI samples

claims.text: K. pneumoniae ciprofloxacin resistance: 17.8% CAUTI vs 11.4% non-CAUTI.
P. aeruginosa cephalosporin (CEF) resistance: 13.7% CAUTI vs 8.1% non-CAUTI.
P. aeruginosa piperacillin (PIP) resistance: 14.5% CAUTI vs 9.8% non-CAUTI.
